title: p-value as a named tail probability under a null
dek: Wikipedia p-value: P(as or more extreme | H0). Not P(H0|data), not a posterior, not an effect size.
story: A p-value on Wikipedia is a tail probability under a specified null and a specified discrepancy: the chance of seeing a statistic this large or larger if H0 were true. It is not the probability that H0 is true.
stats-lrt, Wald/score, and GWAS all emit p-values. This card is the encyclopedia object so a methods section that treats p<0.05 as a posterior odds can be sent here first.
ASA-style warnings are deserved: a p-value does not measure effect size, does not survive silent multiple testing, and does not replace a design.
deep: Change the discrepancy (two-sided vs one-sided, Wald vs LRT) and the p-value changes.
Very large n makes tiny p for tiny effects — scientific importance is extra.
Optional stopping without a plan wrecks the null sampling distribution.

visual.caption: A null sampling density of a statistic, with a tail. The number p is that tail's probability, not a posterior mass on H0.
